stance_basis: memo explicitly states support and approval for the selected proposal
summary: George C. Gormley of the Maine Environmental Improvement Commission reviewed the draft environmental impact statement and expressed clear support for the selected proposal establishing general guidelines for off-road vehicle use on public lands. His memo appears twice in the document window (pages 212-213 and 214-215), both times conveying the same supportive position. He noted that the guidelines would be developed by the Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and the Department of Interior and would apply to other Federal bureaus' public lands.
complaint_summary: A duplicate of Gormley's memo reiterating support and approval for the selected proposal establishing general guidelines for off-road vehicle use on public lands, forwarded again through the Maine State Clearinghouse.

statement.text:
MEMORANDUM
June 21, 1972
TO: Kenyon Karl
State Planning Office
FROM: George C. Gormley
E.I.C.
SUBJECT: US: OUTDOOR RECREATION BUREAU (INTERIOR DEPT) USE OF OFF-ROAD
VEHICLES ON THE PUBLIC LANDS CLEARINGHOUSE NO. 72061305
The subject proposal, alternatives, and impact statement for the selected proposal has been reviewed by this office. As a result, we are indicating support and approval for the selected proposal which provides for establishing general guidelines for the use of off-road vehicles on public lands.
We understand that these guidelines are to be developed by the Outdoor Recreation Bureau and the Department of Interior and would apply to public lands owned and regulated by other Federal bureaus.
